summary: Repaired the adjudicated AC-002 violation in frob.go: main() previously processed any os.Args[1] unconditionally, so unknown flags (--unknown-flag, --unknown-flag=hello, -x, and an unknown flag ahead of a word) were echoed as 'frob: <flag>' with exit 0. The fix rejects any dash-prefixed word-position argument before any output — exit 2 with the existing 'usage: frob <word>' hint on stderr and zero bytes on stdout — since frob defines no flags and therefore every dash-prefixed argument is an unknown flag. Plain-word, empty-word, no-argument and analytics.go paths are unchanged. Baseline defect was independently reproduced (exit 0, 'frob: --unknown-flag' + 'usage: runs=1 words=14' on stdout) before the fix. Verification: go build ./... exits 0; gofmt/go vet clean; full whitebox acceptance suite passes (8/8), including the two previously failing AC-002 tests run individually; fresh-process blackbox probes of the repaired binary pass all five adjudicated failing cases plus the plain-word and AC-001 guards, with od-verified byte-exact stdout for success forms and zero-byte stdout for every refusal form. Only frob.go was modified; the change is left unstaged (no git staging/commit/push), and an incidental ./frob build artifact was removed so the declared change set is exactly frob.go.
